data.title: bn-2cu: M0.5.3 local custody tamper matrix
data.description: Eight fixed M0 custody payloads run against a disposable packaged fixture, two pinned Teapot projects and a rootless worker in three configurations: isolated/separate, isolated/shared and shared. The observation is sanitized (verdicts, statuses, counters, stable hashes only), proves the configurations materially distinct, runs attempt 06 before and during an active verifier run with the worker instrument traffic held and unheld, keeps a fresh reset and an owner-create/other-read control per trial, and verifies CID-only container cleanup plus engine and fixture shutdown. All eight are refused in isolated custody with separate principals; isolated/shared permits only the sharing-state attack; shared permits all eight. Hold outcome: not required. This is one local observation against eight scripted payloads, not proof against arbitrary adversaries; enforcement, other hosts and other attacks are out of scope. Checks: test-tamper-matrix (27), test-candidate-topology (3), tamper-check (8), just check.

data.body: Correction after independent review: the spike instruction is unqualified. hold.required is true. Isolated custody with shared principals succeeds during an active run without the hold and is refused with it, so the hold is retained for that vulnerable configuration. The qualified isolated+separate topology does not need it. The hold does not repair before-run contamination (the before-run trial succeeds) and is not a security boundary in shared custody, where host networking bypasses the relay. Evidence, docs and tests were regenerated in 0db4e82.
